title: Fix the greedy word wrapper (runes, paragraphs, long words) (Go)
prompt: wrap.Wrap(text, width) in wrap.go produces bad output for our CLI help text. It should: return an error when width < 1; keep paragraphs (separated by one or more blank or whitespace-only lines) and emit them separated by exactly one empty line, dropping leading/trailing blank lines; inside a paragraph collapse all whitespace (including newlines and tabs) to single spaces and fill lines greedily so that every line is at most `width` characters, where characters are Unicode code points (runes), not bytes — a line of exactly `width` is fine; never leave trailing spaces; and break a word longer than `width` into width-sized pieces, starting it on a new line, with the last piece continuing as the current line (later words may join it if they fit). Whitespace-only input gives "". Currently lines come out too short, non-ASCII text wraps too early, paragraphs are merged and long words overflow. Run `go test ./...`.
